title: The Long Burn Where Smoke Learned to Settle

features.name: post-fire checkpoint
features.desc-on-touch: you stand where the old servo was — now just a black frame, the roof beams still settling. someone's left a thermos here. the coffee inside is still warm.

features.name: rebuilt shelter
features.desc-on-touch: corrugated iron, three walls, open to the east. the town's rebuilding center — people come here to sort what they've kept.

features.name: ash-layer reading
features.desc-on-touch: the fire burned so long it wrote itself into the earth. you can read the duration in the depth: the longer the smoke stayed, the more it pressed down.

features.name: wire still glowing
features.desc-on-touch: power lines came down but didn't let go. after the fire the town's still connected, just by charred copper and ash. power keeps running through what burned.

features.name: the vigil stone
features.desc-on-touch: people touch this at dawn and dusk. it's not marked. they just know.

inscription: smoke settles where fire cannot; this place learned to breathe in ash; the town burns the same dream again because forgetting is cheaper than remembering

file.name: Post_Fire_Poster_Fading_1987.txt
file.note: a theatre group's announcement of a performance — never happened. corrupted to read: 'The Surgery Where Ashes Learned to Sing — one night only — cancelled by wind'

reverie.title: REVERIE — after the longest burn
narr: you sit on the warm hood of the truck, the ground
still breathing heat. she's writing in a notebook,
pencil shaking. 'it didn't hurt,' she says. 'the fire
was kind. it let things go at their own pace.' the
ash falls like snow, each piece a small forgetting.
you both know the town will burn again. you both stay.

exits.label: back down through the ash-layer, the year the fire lasted longest
where the fire learned to breathe in one direction only
into the older burn, the one the town forgot
